notes_for_editor: Thin web record; no newspapers or board reports on the station itself beyond two Marine reports. Disagreements left in text: tower material (brick vs stone clad in sheet metal), height (9.15/12.6/15 m), Dube dates, date of deactivation of the old light. Parks Canada DFHD pages returned only placeholders, so the 1861 date in the record is attributed to Route des phares. Keeper dates from LighthouseFriends (facts only) are not independently verified. Lighthouse Directory says new light inactive since 2025-12; unverified. Report-year labels for Marine reports follow the corpus labelling. Fact-check 2026-10-27: tower open/closed disagreement (LighthouseFriends vs Directory, which describes the skeletal tower) now stated in Today. Alphonse Richard matched inline in OCR text in both the 1908 and 1909 lists.
